title: The Thirst of the Soul and the Divine Springs
english: Having come to be. Ps 40:14 Blessed indeed is the one whom the Lord blesses, and blessed means that which is worthy of being blessed eternally. Since the one is being blessed by the God of Israel, the 'may it become' prays 'may it become'; not that the prayer makes God blessed, just as neither the name of God is sanctified by the prayer of those saying, 'Hallowed be thy name.' This was said concerning these things in the previous parts.

Ps 41:1 But the three sons of Kore were arranged with others to sing the awesome psalms, which the Scripture also calls hymns, in which also the names are carried in Chronicles. So not the three, being equipped with the same mind and the same judgment, having been united in that which agrees concerning all things, in a unified way pronounce all things in the present psalm.

Ps 41:2a The deer, a creature warring against the eyes and eating them, if ever, having eaten, were to burn from the approaching venom of the serpent, seeks with haste the springs of water to quench the thirst. But those saying that she who wishes to see herself in the waters traces the springs, so that she might know the pollution having happened to her from the blood of the eyes, so that she might cleanse it; for in the scattering of the eyes, they sprinkle the divine blood into it. And the holy one, not lifting up the eyes against serpents and scorpions by which he received authority from Jesus, but also avenging every disobedience, being a spiritual deer, hastens to track out divine springs of water, since the God says, 'You abandoned me, a spring of living water' (Jer 2:13), and concerning the savior it is said to someone, 'You abandoned the spring of wisdom' (Prov 5:2), and the Holy Spirit concerning whom the Word announced, 'I will cause him to drink from the water, I will give to him; there shall be made in him a spring of water springing up unto eternal life' (John 4:14). Perhaps also every inspired Scripture proves to be a saving spring.

Ps 41:3 The intention of the diligent toward God is like that of the deer toward the springs of water with longing. And since they, in the present life, through a mirror, present him to God, having the face to face set aside for the things after this, pray that a time may be established through which, having come, he might appear before the face of God. And it is: since a shadow...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Sea of Life and the Mercy of God
english: As it is said that the law contains the things of the future, the festivals according to the flesh were seen as shadows and symbols of future festivals; one prays to come into the spiritual festivals, so that the face of God may be seen perfectly, being nothing other than the icon of the invisible God.

He who does not toil in vain with tears but from a disposition for the sake of virtue, his own tears shall be fed as a just reward; he calls the day not only in the bearable circumstances but also names the night in the accidental circumstances (Ps 41:4a-b). Those deceived in all things stumble, and concerning the thinking that God is in a place; mocking indeed they say, 'Where is your God?' (Ps 41:4b-5a). For after this desire, you comforted my spirit and the being mocked by those holding me as if there were no helper; and besides these, the memory of the things being performed in those places is for my healing. And 'These things I remembered, and I poured out my soul' instead of 'From despondency I was dissolving' (Ps 41:5a).

Since I am progressing and not yet perfect, and the tabernacle is a symbol of progress as it is often said, for this reason I am troubled; but the tabernacle according to God wonderfully bears upon His own dwelling, that is, the perfection through which we dwell in God (Ps 41:5bc). I shall pass through a wonderful place of tabernacling, as the dwelling of God, in a voice of rejoicing and holy confession according to the manner of those celebrating spiritually; for those celebrating spiritually hear themselves rejoicing and confessing (Ps 41:5bc).

If I were in the land of the Jordan, that is, if I were made worthy of the holy baptism, I will remember your victories (Ps 41:7b). And they also interpret 'Hermon' as the way of the lamp, as the holy baptism opening for them a way of light and radiance into the mind and heart.

The deepest words about Him are the waterfalls of God, or the divine prophets (Ps 41:8). The teaching of this Jesus calls upon the abyss, calling upon the abyss from the Old Scripture. Perhaps also, since the judgments of God are a great abyss, it is presented what is said of the judgments of others as judgments, and even those of all others are from the word of God, which is said to be a small stream (Ps 41:8).

Having the cause; for the God Word is a great sea, but a small sea through which he voluntarily remained in a state of emptying for our sake. All your billows and your waves have passed over me. The sea, which is tropical to human life, not shipwrecked in it but sailing uprightly, having experienced storms and the swellings from the winter of the sea, having arrived at the harbor of salvation, will say the verse: 'For they did not pass over me, but they passed over' (Ps 41:9a).

We have all deeply sought God manifestly as merciful, but not all of us see how he shows mercy; for often, those things occurring according to his mercy, those experiencing them painfully and not sweetly, we think they are not mercy. But he who has deeply sought, whatever God brings, he brings advantageously, that one will not say such a thing as 'Why have you forgotten me?' (Ps 41:10), unless he is discussing his own repentance.

As a dejected one goes gloomily, I inquire what the cause of this is, whether it is from myself or if I shall lift it up through repentance. For we have all deeply sought God manifestly as merciful, even if not all of us see how he shows mercy; for often, those things occurring according to his mercy, those experiencing them painfully and not sweetly, we think they are not mercy, and because of this we say: 'Why have you forgotten me?' (Ps 41:11). The one who has deeply sought, whatever God brings, he brings advantageously, and he will not say such a thing, unless he is discussing his own repentance (Ps 41:12).

Through the advancing bones of the soul, its pleasant doctrines and powers are said to be. Since it often happens to be crushed by terrible sophists, the deceivers reproach, not saying 'Where is your God upon whom you prosper?', but saying to his wisdom that it has been educated, and also concerning this suffering he reasons with his own soul, saying 'Why are you dejected? (Ps 42:5/11) For you hoped to confess upon the Lord; for certainly his face will shine upon you (Ps 42:6/12)', nothing other than the truth, as you are able to loose the deceits of those crushing your set-before bones through the truth from God. If the Lord's face is this, saying: 'But a nation not...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Ears of the Saints and the Horns of Strength
english: They are not [the ears of God] but the ears of men themselves, just as musicians are said to be men. Musical instructions are heard by the ears of musical men. Therefore, when they say 'to our ears' (Ps 43:11), they are not saying it for any other reason but by distinguishing the common things, they say 'to our ears.' The command 'let the one who hears, let him hear' agrees with this.

Our fathers announced to us; those fathers according to instruction announced the divine things, and the ancestors announced what was done through them. 'Your hand has destroyed and planted them' (Ps 43:3b). Regarding the thought of Israel, after the betraying of the Savior from the hand of God, those from the nations, having been destroyed, were planted by divine instruction in the God-breathed writings. God, having maltreated the people of the circumcision, cast them out from the holy training of the law. But the ones from the nations, having conquered not by a law of war, inherited the land spoken of as peaceful. Nor did their own arm save them, that is, their own work. For they have obtained salvation by grace under your right hand and the arm, that is, of the only-begotten Son. 'And the light that finds your face is illumination' (Ps 43:5b); what you have been pleased to save in them by grace, not by their work, so that they should not boast.

The salvation of Jacob, which shakes off the worthless things, is commanded by God to the holy spirits sent for ministry, for those intending to inherit salvation, so that they may quickly arrive at understanding and give help through themselves. Just as God has granted a horn of protection to certain irrational animals so that they may escape those able to harm them, so the horns of Jesus are powers for the saints, goring their enemies. Therefore, also all animals using horns are considered clean, and the food is brought up upon the divine altar.

'God has turned away from himself' (Ps 43:10), not entirely because of sin, but also because of other things for which He is not the cause. And not everyone turning toward the things behind experiences this; for if someone, leaving the worthless things, flees far away by withdrawing from them, not everyone having turned toward the things behind has left what he left behind.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
